claim: Production compilation (merge two rules that fire in sequence, bake the retrieved fact into the new rule) is how declarative instructions become fast task rules; it removes retrieve-and-check steps.
agent_test: Log repeated two-step reasoning patterns in the agent; count how often a merged shortcut would have applied; measure tokens saved on tasks that use it.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Compiled rules start with very low utility and only win after many re-creations (about 100-150 experiences in the dual-task model), so only frequent patterns become routine.
agent_test: Promotion threshold test: promote a lesson to routine after 1, 3 or 10 confirmations; compare accuracy and tokens at equal budget.

claim: Instructions that state pre- and post-conditions beat plain step lists, mainly on hard problems needing adaptation: Exp1 77.0 vs 91.1% (N=31, p=.014), Exp2 78.8 vs 89.0% (N=40, p=.040); effect shrank in Exp3 (N=100, interaction gone). All three experiments are from one lab. In LLMs, no clean test: EffectMem (condition contracts plus checks) gains a lot but mixes format with runtime checks; Xu & Wu 2026 find abstraction level changes small and uncertain (+0.7 and -6.7 pp, CIs cross zero).
agent_test: Store lessons as step lists vs condition-action-outcome form; test on hard held-out items at equal tokens.

claim: Compilation speed is a person-level parameter; one motor-start rule time (0.15 vs 0.35 s) reproduced fast and slow dual-task learners.
agent_test: Not directly testable; low priority.

claim: Compilation cannot merge rules that call the same module, or a perception request with the rule that uses its result, so learned rules end up as perception-to-action steps.
agent_test: Check whether lessons that depend on fresh tool output are wrongly cached as fixed routines.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Compiled rules over-generalise or over-specialise from a single example (DC-10 short runway); error-driven learning is needed to avoid illegal combinations.
agent_test: Commit a routine from 1 example vs 3 examples; measure wrong-reuse rate on near-miss tasks.

claim: Compilation-based transfer (PRIMs) fits human text-editor transfer better than counting identical productions (line editors to Emacs: human 61, identical-productions 39, PRIMs 66 for move-to-line).
agent_test: Store routines at task-general vs task-specific level; test transfer to a related task family.

claim: Practice curves are better fit by an exponential than a power law on unaveraged data (40 data sets, 7,910 series), so the power-law speedup is partly an averaging artefact. Re-opened 2026-11: Heathcote 2000 confirmed (exponential better in 82.2% of series, range 64-93%).
agent_test: Plot tokens per task over repeated use of a routine; fit both forms.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Compilation-style models fit complex-skill data: Kanfer-Ackerman ATC r2 .97/.98/.91/.87 (N=65); past-tense U-shape (model -0.59 vs child -0.34 frequency correlation); dual-task cost vanishing by day 5. All are model fits, mostly by one lab.
agent_test: Supports the mechanism as plausible only; no agent test.

claim: Recent ACT-R work moved away from automatic compilation toward association strength (Ji et al. 2025), and Gianferrara 2021 never switched compilation off; compilation is rarely tested by ablation. Gianferrara 2021 re-opened: N=80 (20 per condition); compilation is a fixed model part that carries across speeds, never switched off.
agent_test: Ablate the routine store (on/off) in our agent: this is the missing ablation.

claim: LLM agents that store verified executable skills gain mostly later in a run and on unseen tasks: Voyager iron tool 21 vs 29 iterations, diamond only with the library (1/3 vs 0/3); early tools no gain. Only 3 runs per method.
agent_test: Routine library on vs off over a long item sequence; compare early and late items.

claim: Verified programmatic skills beat unverified text workflows: ASI 40.4% vs AWM 36.3% vs vanilla 32.7% (WebArena, Claude), steps 5.0 vs 5.9 vs 5.6.
agent_test: Commit lessons only if re-running the trajectory with the lesson succeeds vs commit on any success.

claim: Workflow memory induced from past trajectories raises web-agent success: AWM 35.5% vs 23.5% BrowserGym on WebArena (GPT-4); ReasoningBank 48.8 vs AWM 44.1 vs none 40.5 (Gemini-2.5-flash, re-checked).
agent_test: Compare no memory, success-only workflows, success-plus-failure strategies at equal tokens.

claim: Procedural memory at mixed granularity beat either alone on ALFWorld (GPT-4o test 77.86 vs 56.43 script vs 74.29 trajectory; steps 23.76 to 15.01), but on TravelPlanner hard constraints script (5.50) and proceduralization (9.76) were below no memory (12.88). Re-checked.
agent_test: Test script vs trajectory vs both on tasks with hard constraints; report constraint score separately.

claim: Memory content can hurt: ExpeL full method was worse than retrieval-only on ALFWorld heat tasks; handcrafted insights helped less than LLM ones; reflections added to insight generation hurt. New: SkillsBench self-generated skills -8.1 to -11.5 pp vs none; Liu 2026 weak models fall below no-skill when only general skills are retrievable (Kimi 19.8 vs 21.8; Qwen 19.7 vs 20.5).
agent_test: Report memory gain per task type; gate by type.

claim: Handing skills to models as context does not reliably help: across 8 models skills degrade 15% of tasks (7% Opus 4.6, 25% Qwen3-30B); 39 of 49 SWE skills gave no gain, 3 hurt.
agent_test: Measure routine-in-context vs none per model size; drop routines that do not help.

claim: A strong model writing a reusable tool for a weak model gives large gains (LATM GPT-3.5: Dyck 20.4 to 92.2, word sorting 59.2 to 98.3, Chinese remainder 0 to 100) but vanishes with a strong user model (GPT-4 logical deduction 88.8 to 86.6). Re-checked against Table 2.
agent_test: Test routine value by model strength.

claim: Distilling slow reasoning into direct answers works for some tasks (last letter 30.0 to 98.0) but fails for chain-of-thought maths (GSM8k 36.39 CoT vs 7.13 distilled): a boundary for compiling away steps. Fine-tuning, not scaffold.
agent_test: Do not compile reasoning on multi-step arithmetic-like tasks.

claim: Executable or merged action forms reduce steps: CodeAct up to 20% higher success and 30% fewer actions; ASI cut steps 10.7-15.3%.
agent_test: Allow macro-actions in the scaffold; count turns.

claim: No paper found implements ACT-R-style compilation from repeated co-firing (low start utility, promote after counts) in an LLM agent. Closest: CogRec (Soar chunking after an LLM answers at an impasse; commits after one answer; LLM-call frequency falls) and NeSyPr (trained, ACT-inspired proceduralisation). A 2026 review lists typed impasse-to-rule compilation as an unfilled bundle. Searches (gap round) found no co-firing-count sweep.
agent_test: Build an ACT-R-style routine store (co-firing count, low initial utility) and test against verify-then-commit at equal tokens.

claim: For language agents, writing to procedural memory is riskier than writing to episodic or semantic memory (position paper claim, no experiment). Gap round: still no direct procedural-vs-episodic damage test, but indirect evidence both ways: episodic-only stores match consolidators (Zhang 2026), ungated skill writing equals no skills (GRASP).
agent_test: Inject a wrong lesson into procedural vs episodic memory; measure damage.

claim: A verification or regression gate on skill commits is the main driver of skill-library gains. GRASP: gate removed gives 63.5% (K=4) or 40.1% (K=1, equal to no-skills 40.6%) vs 88.8% with the gate; matched probe budget without using verdicts 70.8%/67.2%. Gate granted to five baselines helped each in-domain, none out of domain.
agent_test: Add a regression check (re-run a few earlier solved cases) before a routine becomes default; compare with write-without-check at equal tokens.

claim: Unverified, model-written skills or ungated consolidation can fall below no-memory. SkillsBench self-generated skills: -8.1, -11.3, -11.5 pp. Zhang 2026: consolidation from ground-truth solutions made GPT-5.4 fail 54% of 19 ARC problems it solved with no memory; ScienceWorld memory peaks near step 20 then falls; WebShop AWM 0.64 (8 examples) to 0.20 (128).
agent_test: Do not merge or rewrite routines after each task; keep raw verified episodes and gate abstraction.

claim: Late-run ablation answer (gap 2): evidence is mixed. Gated promotion (MSCE) improves steadily p0 to p100 (+13.84 to +17.00 Pass@1) and removing crystallisation costs 6.15-11.54 points; ungated consolidation decays after about 20 steps (Zhang 2026). No study controls tokens or gives early vs late split with several runs.
agent_test: Run routine store on/off over a long item sequence; report accuracy by position bucket and total tokens, 3 or more seeds.

claim: More or longer skills do not help: SkillsBench 1 skill +18.0, 2-3 skills +19.0, 4 or more +10.1 pp; compact +19.0, standard +21.5, detailed +14.5, comprehensive +0.7 pp. SkillReducer: 39% body compression with +2.8% quality over 600 skills.
agent_test: Keep each routine short and load at most about 3.

claim: Skill use is fragile in realistic conditions: Claude 55.4% (force-loaded) to 51.2% (agent chooses) to 43.5% (distractors) to 40.1% (retrieved) to 38.4% (no curated); weak models drop below no-skill. Query-specific rewriting recovers part (Claude 40.1 to 48.2) but hurt Kimi (33.5 to 26.7). A cheap predictor of harm was not found.
agent_test: Gate on stated conditions plus a rewrite step; test a self-check of match before use.

claim: Stored-experience format: applicability checks matter more than wording. EffectMem ScienceWorld Qwen3-8B SR 15% to 51% with applicability-gated routing, 65% with execution correction; Xu & Wu: low vs high abstraction +0.7 / -6.7 pp, CIs include zero.
agent_test: Compare condition-checked vs plain-step stores built from the same trajectories.

claim: Cost of writing skills is rarely counted: SkillReducer counts only injection cost (10,000-token skill $0.03-$0.15 per call); GRASP counts probe calls (439 vs 411) but not total tokens; no paper found reports total tokens with the write step at equal budget (gap 9 stays open).
agent_test: Report total tokens including skill induction when testing routines.
